va_spooky_rocks.blurb: Spooky Rocks is a bouldering area in Southwest Virginia, within the High Knob Landform near Keokee Lake. Every climb is a boulder problem, with the bulk between V0 and V5 and a few much harder ones. The problems are split into four sectors: Main Wall (Spooky) holds the most, followed by Around The Bend (Jasper), Bridge Climbing (Three Amigos) and Sharp Block (Standards). The rock here is pebbly and sharp, so skin takes a beating. The High Knob area as a whole is among the rainiest and snowiest in Virginia.

wa_lower_town_wall.blurb: Lower Town Wall is the main cliff above the town of Index, in the Skykomish Valley of the Central-West Cascades. The climbing is nearly all trad, with a handful of sport lines, and the Main Wall mixes single-pitch cracks with multi-pitch routes. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with most between 5.10 and 5.12. The granite at Index is hard on the fingertips. The wall's multi-pitch routes get plenty of sun, and across Index the cliffs are mostly south-facing, so spring, fall and winter can have good days, while summer offers shady spots at midday. The sectors holding the most climbs are Dwarf Tossing to Narrow Arrow, Narrow Arrow and further right, and Great Northern Slab.

wa_other_skagit_valley_crags.blurb: Other Skagit Valley Crags groups the crags of the Skagit Valley outside the main North Cascades areas, in the Northwest Region of Washington. Cumberland Crags, near Mount Vernon, holds nearly all the climbs, and a small bouldering area sits near Big Rock. Trad is the main style, with a good amount of sport and a few boulder problems. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a few at 5.12. At Cumberland the walls offer cracks, bolted slabs and overhangs, rock quality ranges from bomber to choss, and many walls carry black lichen.

bc_doctors_group.blurb: Doctors' Group is a collection of crags within Skaha Bluffs, a climbing area on a hillside above Skaha Lake, just south of Penticton in the Okanagan. Skaha's rock is mostly coarse-grained gneiss. Here the climbing is mainly sport, with a solid share of trad, and it suits climbers at 5.10 and above, with Fern Gully the exception. Grades center on 5.10 to 5.12, with a few 5.13s and only a handful of easier routes. Between the crags there is shade at almost any hour of the day, and Tsunami Wall and Doctors' Wall allow wet-weather climbing most days. Doctors' Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Fern Gully and The Prow.

ca_clark_canyon.blurb: Clark Canyon is a sport climbing area in the Eastern Sierra near Mammoth Lakes, in Mono County. The rock is volcanic tuff, full of holes and pockets, and the routes are short, steep and bolted. Walls face every direction, so sun or shade is easy to find, and the canyon is a place to escape summer heat. Nearly all of the climbing is sport, with a little trad and bouldering. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with most between 5.8 and 5.10 and a spread of moderates. Area 13 and Main Island hold the most climbs, followed by Potato Patch, Parking Lot Rock and The Wave.

ca_oz_area.blurb: The OZ Area lies in the Pinto Basin of Joshua Tree National Park, a part of the park with a decidedly different feel from the more western areas. It is lower in elevation, and some crags sit next to the road while others take a 30 to 45 minute walk over rough, rocky ground. Trad is the main style, with a good amount of sport, a few top-rope routes and some boulders. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.13, with most between 5.7 and 5.10 and a decent spread of moderates. OZ proper holds the most climbs, followed by Magic Mountain Area and Hollywood Area.
